overview: The abilities packet carries the client's fly toggle and speed multipliers, but the vanilla server ignores every flag except isFlying. Server-side anticheats therefore treat C13 as a state signal: it tells them when the player believes they are allowed to fly, which they must reconcile against the abilities the server actually granted. Movement checks such as creative fly, nofall and vertical speed use this state to decide which physics model applies. Because the client can send the toggle out of order relative to the server abilities packet, modern anticheats confirm the state change with a transaction before trusting it.

checks.name: Abilities state handler (Grim)
checks.purpose: Reconciles the client's fly toggle with the server's granted abilities and punishes players who keep flying after the server revoked flight.
checks.how_it_works: Listens for both the inbound PLAYER_ABILITIES packet and the outbound server abilities packet. On the inbound side it sets the player's isFlying flag only if the server allows flight, so a spoofed toggle cannot enable flight. On the outbound side it sends a transaction, and when the server revokes flight it schedules a netty task: if the client has not confirmed the transaction within maxFlyingPing (default 1000 ms), the player is set back for still flying. The comment in the file explains that ability packets can arrive out of order, so the state change is applied on a later tick.
checks.detects: Flight toggles sent while the server has revoked the ability, fly disablers that keep the client airborne after losing flight, and creative fly abuse.
checks.variations: NoCheatPlus feeds the same state into CreativeFly and SurvivalFly through MovingFlying, Hydro keeps a ConfirmedAbilities clone in its lag-compensated packet state, and Intave tracks the toggle in its AbilityTracker. FlopAC wraps the packet as WrappedInAbilitiesPacket, and CheaterDeleter reads the Bukkit isCreative and isFallFlying state instead of the raw packet.

checks.name: CreativeFly (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Vertical and horizontal envelope check for creative and spectator players, where flying is legal and the survival flight model does not apply.
checks.how_it_works: Runs on every move while the player is in creative or spectator mode or is flying. It builds a ModelFlying from the move data, computes a horizontal limit from the fly speed attribute, the flySpeed sent in the abilities packet, sprint modifiers and air friction, and a vertical limit per direction: ascend, descend and hold altitude. Distance beyond the limits accumulates creativeFlyVL; queued velocity can consume the violation. On cancel it returns a setback location, corrected if it exceeds the world height.
checks.detects: Creative fly speed hacks, vertical fly cheats in creative and spectator, and flying above the world height.
checks.variations: Grim handles the same state in its FlightA and NoFall checks via the abilities handler, Hydro in FlightA, and CheaterDeleter in VerticalCheck and SpeedCheck, all keyed off the same can-fly state.

checks.name: ConfirmedAbilities (Hydro)
checks.purpose: Lag-compensated copy of the client's ability flags used by Hydro's movement and emulation checks.
checks.how_it_works: A small plain class holding godMode, flying, flightAllowed, creativeMode, walkSpeed and flySpeed. Hydro stores a ConfirmedAbilities instance in the packet state, updates it from the inbound abilities packet, and clones it when the server sends abilities so checks read what the client believes its abilities are at a given tick. The clone method lets the emulation engine snapshot state before applying a move.
checks.detects: Provides the state needed to detect flight abuse and creative fly where the client's view of its abilities diverges from the server's.
checks.variations: Grim's PacketPlayerAbilities and Intave's AbilityTracker implement the same idea with transaction confirmation; Hydro's version is a pure state clone.

checks.name: AbilityTracker (Intave)
checks.purpose: Tracks the abilities state server-side so the movement simulator knows whether flight is legal for the player.
checks.how_it_works: Registers receiveAbilities and sentAbilities handlers. On the inbound abilities packet it stores the requested flying flag and, only if the server had allowed flying, sets the player's flying state; otherwise it records disabledFlying. The sentAbilities side compares the new server state against the previous one and, when flight is revoked, requires the player to confirm the teleport rate limit before treating the player as grounded again. The tracker is consumed by the Physics simulation checks.
checks.detects: Flying without the server granting the ability, and clients that ignore a flight revocation.
checks.variations: Grim confirms the same revocation with a transaction timeout, NCP with the CreativeFly and SurvivalFly envelope, and Hydro with a plain state clone.
